Subject: Renewal & mid-cycle top-up options — staged top-up / co-term paths

Hi Jill / Samir,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a draft SOW (Orchard_SOW_v3.pdf) and a short usage report for Q1 so you can see where the bulk of generation hours are landing.

We heard two priorities from your side: predictability for budgeting, and a path to add capacity mid-term without breaking the renewal cadence. To make that concrete, I wanted to propose three ways to handle the uplift and co-term:

- Option A — Staged top-up (recommended): add incremental capacity in two tranches this quarter; newly added capacity is billed at a 10% discounted uplift rate if Orchard commits to a 12-month add-on term aligned to the existing renewal.
- Option B — One-time mid-contract top-up: immediate uplift at standard uplift pricing; invoice pro-rated to month boundary; no co-term discount.
- Option C — Annualize now, true-up later: convert anticipated uplift into an annualized commitment now with a slightly higher up-front credit, and true-up based on actual usage at next renewal.

Can you confirm which path you prefer? If you want, we can run a quick numbers sheet for A vs C to show monthly spend impact. If procurement prefers a PO approach, loop them in and we can provide a short addendum instead of a full amendment.

Next steps: if you like Option A I’ll circulate the amended SOW and a DocuSign link for the add-on so legal can sign quickly.

Thanks,

Mateo — quick model attached (staged_topup_model.xlsx). High-level output below:

- Option A (Staged top-up):
  - Immediate invoice month: baseline charge + pro-rated 250k uplift at 9% off list (effective uplift discount because we apply 10% to incremental rate; blended monthly increase ~ +$11,200).
  - Month 4 (once second tranche hits): blended invoice shows total uplift +$19,800/month vs baseline. 6-month incremental spend (months 1–6) = ~+$65,600.
  - Suggested contract language: "Customer may add incremental capacity in up to two tranches as described; incremental units billed at uplift rate with a 10% add-on discount when add-on is committed for 12 months and co-terminates with the base agreement."

- Option B (One-time mid-contract top-up):
  - Immediate uplift billed pro-rata at standard uplift rate (no co-term discount). 6-month incremental spend = ~+$78,400.

- Option C (Annualize now):
  - Convert expected uplift into an annualized add-on now; grant a 6% higher credit up-front versus Option A but requires annual commitment; 6-month spend profile is highest up-front but lowest month-to-month predictability risk. 6-month incremental spend = ~+$71,000 (after credit amortization).

Recommendation: Option A balances Orchard’s cashflow concerns and our desire for committed runway. If they sign the 12-month add-on co-term we can offer the 10% uplift discount on incremental units only; blended discounts only apply if they convert more of the baseline to a committed level (rare).

I also added a short PO addendum template in the workbook and a sample DocuSign text.

—Lauren
